newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE wheat rises as sterling turns down.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE wheat rises as sterling turns down.

text.p: Sterling's new found weakness pushed LIFFE wheat higher, traders said.

By late Friday sterling was down almost ten pfennigs against the week's peak, reaching less than 2.74 marks. It had been sent reeling by reports that the new government wanted it in the European exchange rate mechanism at 2.50 marks.
July was the most active month, with 201 lots done of a total 723. It last traded 1.20 stg higher at 94.75 stg.
On the new crop November traded 198 lots, ending 0.90 stg higher at 97.50 stg.

The aftermath of a holiday on the continent on Thursday and moribund physical markets, partly because of the absence of some important players at the Corn Exchange Bourse in London, militated against active trade.
Even so, the 723 lots of wheat done can be called anything but high against the background of recent record volume.
The amount of grain changing hands on the delivered market was minimal, physical traders said.
